methodological_rigor.justification: In vivo preclinical study using two murine tumor models (B16-F10 melanoma in C57BL/6 and 4T1 breast in BALB/c), clinically relevant HDR brachytherapy with Ir-192 and CT-based dose planning, and thoughtful mechanistic dissection via CD8+/CD4+/NK cell depletion. Strengths include the causal depletion experiments showing CD8+ is essential, re-challenge experiments suggesting immunological memory, and appropriate ethical/ARRIVE framing. Weaknesses: small group size (n=5 per group), no randomization or blinding stated, no sample-size justification, multiplicity corrections not applied across many group comparisons, and descriptions of tumor volumes in the text (e.g., 127 vs 1425 mm3) lack variance/CI reporting. Statistics use Shapiro-Wilk, Levene, ANOVA/Tukey or Kruskal-Wallis, and Mantel-Cox with p<0.05, which are appropriate but basic.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical murine in vivo study maps to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is plausible: IMQ is FDA-approved topically, brachytherapy is standard in several indications, and small case series/phase I-II trials combining topical IMQ with RT exist (refs 26, adams). However, the specific intratumoral normalizing-dose IMQ + HDR BT sequence requires human validation, dose translation, and safety data before clinical adoption, so translation is plausible but not demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal study where ARRIVE is the applicable standard; authors explicitly reference ARRIVE compliance in Supplementary Materials. Materials are well documented (cell lines, antibodies, equipment, treatment planning system). Gaps include: missing explicit reporting of randomization, blinding, and allocation concealment; no formal sample-size calculation; the number of independent experiments is not clearly stated; and only n=5 per group per experiment is reported. Data availability score is 2 because no raw data, analysis scripts, or public repository are mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: Combining TLR7 agonists with radiotherapy has been examined in multiple studies (refs 6, 24, 25), and topical IMQ + brachytherapy has been used in case series (ref 26). The authors' prior publications (refs 5, 7) established IMQ vascular normalization and 10 Gy BT as in-situ vaccination. The novelty here is the specific synergy demonstration in two tumor models with mechanistic CD8+ dependence and memory on re-challenge. This is a meaningful but incremental extension of the authors' own program rather than a first-in-class concept.

writing_presentation.justification: Introduction and discussion clearly frame the 'seventh R' of radiobiology concept and IMQ's dual immunostimulant/antiangiogenic role. However, the text has noticeable language and punctuation issues (em-dashes throughout, occasional grammar slips, e.g., 'IMQ sensitizing brachytherapy'), some claims in results are numerical without dispersion estimates, and one paragraph references 'Adams et al.' without a formal citation. Overall readable but would benefit from editorial tightening.

key_strengths: Mechanistically informative depletion experiments demonstrate CD8+ T cells are essential for the combination effect, with NK/CD4+ depletion paradoxically enhancing efficacy
Two tumor models tested—immunogenic (B16-F10) and poorly immunogenic (4T1)—with complete regression in 20% of 4T1 mice and immune memory on re-challenge
Clinically translatable HDR Ir-192 brachytherapy with CT-based planning and documented dose distribution
Explicit ethical oversight and ARRIVE compliance stated
key_concerns: Small group sizes (n=5) with no power calculation or report of biological replicate number
No randomization or blinding described; selection bias cannot be ruled out
No multiplicity correction across numerous group comparisons (tumor growth, blood counts, infiltrates, depletion arms)
Novelty is incremental—builds on authors' own prior work (refs 5, 7) and overlaps with published TLR7+RT combinations
One reference ('Adams et al.') is cited in text without a bibliographic entry in the reference list shown
Data and analysis code are not shared
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid proof-of-concept preclinical study with clear mechanistic support but limited by sample size and incremental novelty; appropriate for a specialty Tier 3 journal after minor revisions improving statistical reporting and resolving the unreferenced Adams et al. citation.
